title: Node capacity rollforward weekly export
content:
Sheet export: Node Capacity Rollforward — weekly snapshot
Date: 2026-11-22
Source: capacity-dashboard -> node-level pivot (7d window)
Export notes: CSV-style table below is a direct pull from the pivot with computed fields (7d_avg_util, headroom_1hr_est, fragmentation_pct). Headroom_1hr_est assumes steady-state demand at 95th percentile spot load. Burst_Credits are normalized per-node available credits.

Columns:

Summary pivot metrics (computed):
- Fleet 7d-weighted avg util: 61%
- Fleet 95th percentile peak (24h windows): 88%
- Nodes above alert threshold (>90% 7d_avg): 4 nodes (node-a-104, node-e-302, node-c-006, node-j-013)
- High fragmentation nodes (fragmentation_pct > 40%): 4 nodes (node-b-210, node-d-501, node-f-122, node-i-412)
- Idle-reservations candidates (active_slices / allocated_slices < 0.35): node-b-210, node-d-501, node-i-412
- Spot-scale-down candidates (avg util < 20% && burst_credits > 200): node-d-501

Regional rollups:
- us-west: weighted avg util 58%, headroom risk at peak windows (3 nodes flagged)
- us-east: weighted avg util 49%, batch backfill tapering will free ~740 slices next week
- eu-west/eu-central: weighted avg util 72%, several dedicated nodes near SLO limits
- ap-southeast: weighted avg util 19%, opportunity to consolidate spot footprint

Computed action items (owner suggestions):
1) (Action) Investigate node-a-104 and node-e-302 hotspots: enable canary spill to pool-burst for 2-hour window and monitor error/latency (owner: Daniel Kim, Jira: INFRA-4221).
2) (Action) Create reservation reclamation ticket for nodes with high fragmentation: tag node-b-210, node-f-122, node-i-412 for slice compaction experiment (owner: Marcus Liu).
3) (Action) Schedule scale-down for spot nodes in ap-southeast next maintenance window if not used during business hours (owner: Sofia Ramirez).
4) (Monitoring) Add a new alert rule: 7d_avg_util > 88% AND headroom_1hr_est < 10% -> Pager for SRE (proposal in confluence://infra/capacity-rollforward-2026Q4).

Open questions / caveats:
- Headroom formula assumes linear demand growth for 1hr; may under/overestimate microburst tolerance for services using KV cache reuse.
- Fragmentation metric is coarse; slice packing heuristics change next release (see PR #789 on infra repo).
- Some H100 nodes report slightly higher peak telemetry latency; correlate with kernel selection logs before taking node OOS.

Quick timeline suggestions:
- This week: apply spill canary for latency pools; run compaction job on 5% of high-frag nodes as experiment.
- Next week: re-evaluate reserved vs shared split for us-east batch (expected free slices ~740).

Reference snippets from pivot calculations:
- headroom_1hr_est_pct = max(0, 100 - (95th_pct_peak * safety_factor)) where safety_factor = 1.0 for committed, 1.15 for spot
- fragmentation_pct = 100 * (1 - active_slices / allocated_slices) (clipped at 0)

Notes to reviewers: this export is intended to be a single-source snapshot to feed the capacity-runbook playbook. Please comment inline in the sheet or on Slack thread linked above.

End of export.
